purpose: Expose principal-level reasoning for LIMS and ELN vendor evaluation through questions, mechanisms, field evidence, and repair paths.

level_contract.focus: failure, recovery, and operational edge cases

probes.title: Specimen lifecycle and correction semantics
probes.question: Can the platform preserve the original scientific record while corrections, revisions, and downstream projections converge on one explainable current state?
probes.material_effect: Scientists can trust the current view and reconstruct how it changed.
evaluation_levels: Describe the visible correction experience.
Trace identity, occurrence time, recording time, revision, actor, and reason.
Exercise a correction and independent readback with synthetic records.
Recover from concurrent correction, downstream timeout, and replay.
Compare vendor audit exports with the canonical lifecycle contract.

probes.title: Custody under concurrency
probes.question: Can two competing specimen movements preserve one current location and a complete transfer history?
probes.material_effect: Laboratory teams can locate material and understand conflicts from the durable custody record.
evaluation_levels: Locate a specimen and its current custody position.
Explain the transaction boundary for position and event.
Exercise concurrent transfers against one source revision.
Recover from ambiguous write and stale revision.
Compare latency, audit detail, offline handling, and operational ergonomics.

probes.title: Instrument ingress and raw artifact fidelity
probes.question: Can every parsed observation resolve to the exact received bytes, parser version, disposition, and recovery path?
probes.material_effect: Scientific reviewers can distinguish source data from derived interpretation.
evaluation_levels: Identify raw artifact and parsed observation surfaces.
Trace byte digest, media type, parser version, and observation identity.
Exercise complete, partial, duplicate, and changed-byte transfers.
Resume interrupted transfer while preserving evidence.
Compare instrument protocols, storage limits, and reprocessing support.

probes.title: Configured vendor conformance
probes.question: Can Sapio, Benchling, LabKey, or another candidate express the canonical specimen graph through supported interfaces and reproduce it through independent readback?
probes.material_effect: Evaluators can separate documented compatibility from configured and exercised capability.
evaluation_levels: Name the supported product, API, and SDK versions.
Map canonical identity, relationships, measurements, artifacts, and audit fields.
Run the representative graph in a configured environment.
Exercise rate limits, partial batches, duplicate events, and export.
Compare upgrade path, portability, support model, and mapping complexity.

probes.title: Transactional event delivery
probes.question: Can a domain change and its integration event commit atomically while mature connector infrastructure handles transport?
probes.material_effect: Downstream systems receive stable events through established connector, replay, and observability capabilities.
evaluation_levels: Identify which business events cross service boundaries.
Explain the aggregate, event, and outbox transaction.
Exercise publication, duplicate delivery, and consumer replay.
Measure connector lag and recover from broker or consumer interruption.
Compare CDC support, payload evolution, operating cost, and vendor integration fit.

probes.title: Flyway migration and semantic reconciliation
probes.question: Can parallel database changes reach one catalog while representative data preserves identity, scientific meaning, relationships, and artifacts?
probes.material_effect: Application releases can proceed independently while the data model remains explainable and recoverable.
evaluation_levels: Name the migration set and supported PostgreSQL majors.
Explain Flyway history, transaction, and naming behavior.
Exercise clean install and populated predecessor upgrade.
Exercise late merge, transactional failure, replay, and forward correction.
Compare catalog, data reconciliation, lock impact, and release compatibility.

probes.title: Restore and data exit
probes.question: Can a clean environment reconstruct records, metadata, roles, artifacts, configuration references, and integration position within declared objectives?
probes.material_effect: Continuity and vendor portability become demonstrated capabilities rather than contract assumptions.
evaluation_levels: List the components required for recovery.
Explain ordering, keys, identity dependencies, and integration restart position.
Run a clean restore with representative data.
Recover from an unavailable latest backup and measure resulting RPO.
Compare RTO, RPO, automation, export fidelity, and operator burden.

probes.title: Scientific data primitives across boundaries
probes.question: Do API models, transfer objects, events, database columns, exports, and vendor mappings preserve the same temporal, identity, decimal, unit, vocabulary, JSON, and null semantics?
probes.material_effect: Technical and scientific evaluators can find semantic loss before migration or vendor commitment.
evaluation_levels: Identify each primitive and its scientific meaning.
Trace one value through ingress, DTO, event, persistence, API, and export.
Exercise timezone, decimal, unit, Unicode, null, and boundary fixtures.
Repair a lossy vendor mapping and prove round-trip fidelity.
Compare representational limits, portability, queryability, and maintenance cost.
